title: Finite schemes as limits of finite finitely presented closed models
statement: Let $S$ be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] and $p:T\to S$ a finite morphism [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. Then there exist a nonempty directed set $I$, schemes $T_i$ over $S$ with structure maps $p_i:T_i\to S$, compatible transition maps $r_{ji}:T_j\to T_i$ for $j\ge i$, and compatible $S$-morphisms $\pi_i:T\to T_i$, such that each $p_i$ is finite and of finite presentation (locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], quasi-compact and quasi-separated), each $r_{ji}$ is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion], and $(T,(\pi_i))$ is the inverse limit of this system in the category of schemes [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition]. In particular $p_i\circ\pi_i=p$ for every $i$.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-iff-integral-lft], the finite $p$ is integral and locally of finite type. It is affine by [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], hence quasi-compact and quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence](3). Since $S$ is qcqs, [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](2) makes $T$ qcqs. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-lft-limit-closed-fp] to $p$: obtain a nonempty directed inverse system $(T_i)$ with qcqs stages, finite-presentation structure maps $p_i$, closed transitions and compatible $S$-projections $\pi_i$ with limit $T$.

Each $p_i$ is locally of finite type: a finitely presented algebra is generated by the images of the finitely many polynomial variables [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Closed transitions are finite by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-integral-separated-uc](c). All hypotheses of [lem-weil-pbc-eventually-finite] now hold, including integrality of $p$ from step 1. Choose $i_0$ with every $p_i$ finite for $i\ge i_0$.

Restrict to $J=\{i\mid i\ge i_0\}$. It is nonempty and directed. The limit remains $T$: for any cone on the tail and any original index $a$, choose $b\ge a,i_0$ and compose its map to $T_b$ with $r_{ba}$. Two choices agree by passing to a common upper bound; these maps form a cone on the full system, uniquely extending the tail cone. The full limit universal property therefore gives the tail limit property. All stage, transition and compatibility assertions are inherited, including $p_i\pi_i=p$, so this tail proves the statement.
